editorial:
Imagine you are a rich socialite living a fancy life, but then someone starts sending you creepy blackmail letters. That is exactly what happens to Julie Wardh. She is caught in a messy web with three different men: her distant husband, a new guy she is seeing, and a mean ex-boyfriend who seems like he enjoys causing pain. The whole movie feels like a high-stakes game of cat and mouse. You will spend most of your time trying to figure out who is lying and who is actually the killer. It has that classic 70s European style with bright colors and a lot of tension that keeps you on edge.

What really works here is how the movie keeps you guessing. The acting is solid, and the twists are satisfying without being too confusing. While it moves a bit slow in the middle, the payoff at the end is totally worth it. If you love old-school mysteries with a dark side, you should definitely check this out.
endingExplained: The big twist is that the killer is actually George, the friend's cousin who seemed like the nice guy. He used the blackmail letters to trick Julie and make her trust him while framing her ex. In the final scenes, his true colors come out and he tries to kill Julie. After a tense struggle, he is finally stopped, and Julie is safe from the man she thought was her savior.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves vintage murder mysteries and unexpected plot twists.
